row.proto: void Car_Tyre_SetWearFactor(void *tyre_component, bool apply_set, uint16_t force)
row.notes: TyreComponent method, rcx = tyre component. It applies the fitted set's compound to the car; setting the wear factor is one of its steps. It rebuilds the class list at +0x9bd0 through 0x142e9e6c0 when +0x9c58 is null or +0x9c50 differs from +0x9bc0, then picks the fitted set's class entry (0x18 stride, matched on [+0x9c98]-0x6c; when no entry matches, the option 4 entry if that value is >= 3 unsigned, else option 1). Wear factor: 1.0 when the matched value is >= 5, otherwise 0.5 * ([[w0+8]+0x630] + [[w3+8]+0x630]) * [tc+0x98e0+i*4] (w0/w3 = [[veh+0x580]+0x70/+0x88], veh = [[tc+0x20]+0x58]; i = the matched value, the fallback option, or -1 when neither is listed), and 1.0 when that is negative. It writes the factor to +0x80 and [tc+0x98f4] to +0x84 of all four wheels [[veh+0x580]+0x70..+0x88], with the log PITSTOP_TYRES 'Wear factor set to %f on vehicle %d' (vehicle = [veh+0xe8]) when that channel is on; a null [tc+0x20] or veh skips those writes. It then computes the reset flag (force's low byte when force > 0xff, otherwise whether the fitted class at +0x9950 or the set index at +0x9954 changed), stores the new class and index at +0x9950/+0x9954 (one qword store, which also zeroes +0x9955..+0x9957), and only then returns early when [tc+0x20] is null (0x142ea25f1). Then for each of the 4 wheels it formats '%s_%s%c' (0x1457ef36f) from [[[[tc+0x20]+0x58]+0x558]+0x128] (Chassis TyrePhysicsGroup string object +0x118: +0x08 capacity, +0x10 buffer, filled by 0x1446506e0), a code from the class entry and 'f'/'r', lowercases it, finds it in the global compound map ([[[0x1460806d8]+0x50]+0x138], find 0x144776d00) and, when the map value it finds is non-null, passes that value with the reset flag to 0x155436e70 (through the .xtls thunk 0x1446b18e0, rcx = wheel+8). All five call sites of 0x142ea2a90 pass force 0, so that path takes the changed test. With apply_set it uses the set at [+0x9c98]-0x70 instead when the allocation at +0x9c68 is null or the fitted class or index is out of range in it (class < 0 or >= [alloc+0xd8], an empty class list, or index >= the set count). 0x155436e70 rebinds the wheel's compound when the flag is set or the compound changed, and a set flag also resets the temperatures at wheel+0x6c/+0x70/+0x74 (it takes rcx = wheel+8, 0x142ea2630, and stores its +0x64/+0x68/+0x6c). When no class entry matches, the entry stays null and i is -1, so with [tc+0x20] set the wheel loop faults on that null entry (0x142ea26b5, 0x142ea27c1); with [tc+0x20] set and veh null it faults at 0x142ea264e. apply_set != 0: then 0x142e88840 applies the fitted set of the weekend allocation (+0x9c68). Last it posts an event through 0x1439876c0 (0x142ea2a60) carrying [veh+0xe8] and the set index +0x9954. Callers: Car_Tyre_ChangeToNextCompound call 0x142e946b7 with (tc, 1, 0x101); tail jump 0x142ea2da4 from 0x142ea2a90. f1_1990_brand.dll calls it with (tc, true, 0x101) after rewriting the group string. 1.0.145 twin 0x142ea4890, 427/427 instructions the same.
